scope: The thinker cards on the reading route: Aristotle, Spinoza, Nietzsche, Deleuze, Guattari, Land

by.review: Independent reviewer (Claude subagent, fresh context), 2026-10-24, 25 searches and fetches: Aristotle and Spinoza pass; Nietzsche, Deleuze, Guattari and Land pass after fixes now made (the archived Wicks entry added as a source; a repeated sentence on Deleuze's illness; the Guattari source credited to Adam Shatz; Land's move to Shanghai dated loosely, his essay named, and an unquoted run from Burrows reworded). Guattari's analysis with Lacan is left undated, as sources disagree (Britannica: the 1950s; Universalis: until 1960; other accounts 1962–69).

note: Biographical claims were checked against the sources below; claims marked not-retrieved are the card's standard doctrine, which the cited Stanford entry covers but which was not re-read in this pass. Unsupported details were cut and errors corrected.

sources: SEP “Aristotle” (Shields), §§1–5, read through a course's outline of the entry (uvm.edu)
checked: born 384 in Stagira; to Athens c. 367; Academy twenty years until Plato's death (347)
Assos and Lesbos; biological research is 'probably' (the card now says so)
tutor to Alexander; Lyceum 335; Chalcis 323, death 322
about 200 treatises, 31 survive; surviving texts are lecture notes and drafts, the published works, some dialogues, lost
method from appearances, received opinion and puzzles (aporiai); first formal logic; the Organon
fixed: 'doing much of his biological research' made probable and placed at Assos
Alexander's death kept as the occasion, with anti-Macedonian feeling in Athens (reviewer)
not_retrieved: four causes, hylomorphism, soul as form, unmoved mover, ethics and politics paragraphs, reception as First Teacher and the Philosopher

checked: studies cut short at seventeen for the family importing business
herem of 27 July 1656, the harshest the community pronounced
Theological-Political Treatise anonymous, 1670
friends published his writings after his death in 1677; still at work on the Political Treatise
mind as the idea of the body; three kinds of knowledge, the first called 'opinion, or imagination' in the Ethics; conatus; no final causes; intellectual love of God
not_retrieved: reception and interpretive disputes in the last paragraph

sources: the bundled Genealogy of Morals (I §§2, 7; II)
checked: born 1844 in Röcken; father, a minister, died when he was four
Bonn and Leipzig; teaching at Basel from 1869 at twenty-four
friendship with Wagner broke down in 1878 with Human, All Too Human
resigned in June 1879; wandering life 1880–1889; collapse in Turin, January 1889, an invalid thereafter
died 25 August 1900; sister collected the notebooks as The Will to Power; parts espoused by the Nazis partly through her contacts

Birth of Tragedy's Apollonian and Dionysian; God is dead in The Gay Science (1882); Zarathustra; master and slave morality, the revolt of the slaves (GM I §7); creditor and debtor (GM II); ascetic ideals; perspectivism; will to power
fixed: 'before finishing his doctorate' and 'so brilliant' cut (not in the source)
'ended bitterly in the late 1870s' dated to 1878
'boarding houses in Switzerland, Italy and the south of France, writing a book a year' replaced by the wandering years 1880–1889
Elisabeth as 'a nationalist and antisemite whom Nietzsche had opposed', 'a misleading edition' and 'postwar scholarship freed his work' cut as unsourced
not_retrieved: amor fati and the list of values; the influence on existentialism, psychoanalysis, post-structuralism and literature

sources: SEP “Gilles Deleuze” (Smith, Protevi and Voss), §1 and introduction
checked: born in Paris, 18 January 1925; a year of school in Normandy; Pierre Halbwachs at Deauville; brother arrested for resistance, died on the train to Auschwitz
khâgne at Lycée Henri IV; taught by Hyppolite (SEP spells it Hippolyte), Alquié, Canguilhem, de Gandillac
1953–1962 posts, 'a hole in my life'; the respiratory ailment from that period for the rest of his life
first books and dates; married Fanny (Denise Paul) Grandjouan, translator of D. H. Lawrence; two children

doctorat d'État 1968 with Difference and Repetition and the Spinoza thesis; Vincennes/Paris VIII from 1969 to retirement in 1987; met Guattari 1969 (SEP's introduction says 1968); trip to the United States in 1975; 'Immanence: A Life' 1995; took his own life on 4 November 1995
fixed: the Sacher-Masoch date, the 1981 edition of Spinoza: Practical Philosophy and Desert Islands (2002) cut as not found in the source
'severe respiratory illness that made even writing laborious' replaced by the ailment staying with him for life, as SEP has it
not_retrieved: the list of later books and their dates

checked: a radical psychoanalyst and political activist; met Deleuze in 1969 (SEP §1)
fixed: 'in the early 1950s' removed from his analysis with Lacan: not confirmed, and the analysis is usually dated later
not_retrieved: birth date and place; La Borde from 1955 and its institutional psychotherapy; the dissident Communist paper and CERFI; his books; death in 1992. The cited London Review of Books review of Dosse could not be opened here; a fuller check needs it or Dosse's biography.

sources: Nick Land, “A Quick-and-Dirty Introduction to Accelerationism”
checked: Warwick in the 1990s; the CCRU set up by Sadie Plant and led by Land after she left academia
quit the academy in 1998 and moved to China

first monograph on Bataille; Fanged Noumena (2011, Mackay and Brassier); 'Circuitries' and 'Meat'; positive feedback against negative feedback's stabilizing effect, another name for hyperstition; hyperstition as a fiction that makes itself real
Williams: the term coined by Noys; Land answered Anti-Oedipus's question in the affirmative
Land credits the 2013 manifesto with 're-animating the accelerationist question'; the quotation on capitalism's self-awareness, verbatim
Burrows: The Dark Enlightenment; neoreaction rejects democracy, embraces autocratic rule and is anti-egalitarian
fixed: 'in 1995 he and Sadie Plant founded' replaced by Plant setting it up (O'Sullivan); the founding year not confirmed
Noys 'coined' the name: Britannica traces the word to Zelazny's Lord of Light (1967) and credits Noys with its later sense; both now stated
'reawakening the idea' replaced by Land's own words; 'In 2017' dropped (the essay's date not confirmed); the quotation now verbatim
'moved to China' in 1998 made 'later settled in Shanghai', since only Burrows joins the two
not_retrieved: the 2012 date of The Dark Enlightenment
